subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: After template and hook injection is closed, should package-to-dev conversion permanently refuse every pre-existing `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`, including empty directories and valid OpenClaw checkouts?
rationale: Remote inspection cannot make an adopted checkout trustworthy, but unconditional refusal intentionally breaks the previously supported conversion path and requires one-time operator action for existing setups.

options.title: Approve Fresh-Path Only
options.body: Require an unused destination for package-to-dev conversion and document moving the old path or selecting a new one.

options.title: Design Explicit Replacement
options.body: Add a separately approved, destructive replacement flow that never builds or executes the existing directory and clearly protects user data.

options.title: Keep Existing Adoption
options.body: Retain the old compatibility behavior and accept that a canonical-looking local checkout can influence what the updater builds and installs.

recommendation.title: Approve Fresh-Path Only
recommendation.body: Require an unused destination for package-to-dev conversion and document moving the old path or selecting a new one.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most strongly connects this person to the update orchestration and compatibility boundary changed here.
